title: Ziyadid dynasty
capsule: The Ziyadid dynasty, founded c. 819 by Muhammad ibn Ziyad under Abbasid appointment, governed the Tihama coastal plain of western Yemen from its capital at Zabid for roughly two centuries. At its height under Ibrahim ibn Ziyad in the ninth century, the dynasty controlled a prosperous agricultural and maritime trade zone; Zabid became a center of Islamic scholarship. The line weakened through succession disputes in the tenth century and was supplanted by the Najahids, a dynasty of Ethiopian slave-soldiers, around 1018–1021, though Ziyadid nominal presence lingered until the twelfth century.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Ziyadid territorial extent is broadly attested in medieval Arabic geographical sources, but precise boundary delineation of their Tihama holdings is scholarly inference rather than surveyed record.
